gates.title: Is the idea worth building?
criteria: You can explain the idea, its value, and its buyer in two minutes
Competition understood — you know what you do that they cannot copy quickly
Make-or-buy decided and the reason recorded
You are willing to spend real money on this

gates.title: Is the design complete enough to build against?
criteria: Every transaction, flow, journey and domain relationship is documented
Every page has a mock-up — no page enters Build undesigned
MENU.XLS and TABLES.XLS exist and agree with each other
Security matrix answers who can do what to which data
Brand, templates and website theme are settled

gates.title: Does it actually work end to end?
criteria: P0 through P5 complete, each signed off against its own finish line
Every journey runs start to finish with real data
Integrations live, with a defined behaviour on failure
DEV / TEST / PRD exist and the migration path has been run twice
Backups scheduled and a restore has actually been tested

gates.title: Are we safe to put this in front of paying customers?
criteria: Functional, performance and security passes complete
Role-based access tested by trying to see what you should not
Pilot users onboarded and their fix-now list closed
Help content and support path exist and have been used once
Scope frozen; the fast-follow list is published

phases.name: Define
phases.purpose: Decide what you are building and whether it is worth building.
phases.outcome: A value statement you can defend, a competitor read, and a build-or-buy decision.

phases.name: Design
phases.purpose: Describe the whole application on paper before writing a line of code.
phases.outcome: Transactions, flows, journeys, domain model, every page mocked up, security matrix, and a brand.

phases.name: Build
phases.purpose: Stand the company up and construct the application in ordered prototypes.
phases.outcome: A legally real company, a working stack, and P0 through P5 delivered in sequence.

phases.name: Prove
phases.purpose: Attack the application until you trust it, then put it in front of real users.
phases.outcome: Tested journeys, a security pass, documentation, a support path, and a completed pilot.

phases.name: Launch
phases.purpose: Go live deliberately, with a rollback plan and named owners.
phases.outcome: Production cutover, billing that works, a live website, and customer #1 onboarded personally.

phases.name: Operate
phases.purpose: Run it, watch it, and feed what you learn back into Define.
phases.outcome: An operating rhythm, cost control, and a loop back to the top of the method.
